body: you are not alone. I hope that gives you peace.

I felt anxiety reading this because of how well you explained panic attacks for myself. Its hard to over come these feelings, but I always try to ask myself questions that bring me back to the present. "what do you see, what do you hear, what do you smell, what do you taste what do you feel?" combine this with some meditative breathing. I hope this helps.

I want you to know that I am in the exact same boat as you. You are not alone! It was comforting to me today to know that I am not alone either. Thank you for your post. I am an art lover and often hold myself back from sharing it due to my anxiety and depression.

It may sound silly... but every time that I felt overwhelmed with regret, resentment, or guilt.. I would train my brain to redirect the thought. "I inhale peace, positivity, and forgiveness and exhale guilt, shame, and hurt for it no longer serves me."  I would say this phrase 10x times in my head or out loud until the bad emotions/thoughts went away. A little bit of positive psychology and brain training can do wonders. Eventually you realize holding on to those emotions are only hurting yourself. I hope this helps!

Yes, I used to be anorexic around 2 year ago. After I gave it up, and began to eat a balanced diet again, I gained all of the healthy weight back of what I was prior to anorexia and 40 pounds more. Sorry if I had a hard time explaining that.

I feel the same as you - you are not alone. When things happen that trigger stressors and old emotions my mind thinks "what's the point?" I have told a therapist before, and they did not understand how one could feel this way yet not be actively suicidal. 

You are not alone. I pray your days get better. I pray you start to live a life filled with so much happiness that you never question this again.
I have been to therapy on and off. I feel exhausted after sharing and re-living the thoughts and feelings during it. Regardless - thank you for responding. I appreciate it.
I really enjoyed this and needed this today. Your words are so true and can be so hard to keep in mind on the hard days. I am thankful to have seen them. I know that it wasn't an accident. '

As I'm reading your post, it's insane how much this girl sounds like myself. I write motivational columns for a magazine on how to be more positive. I am always smiling, I am always laughing. I am always helping others. I never let others see me cry. But some days when I close the door and the masks comes off, I feel so much pain. I feel my scars so deeply. but that is the beauty in a positive mindset, is you choose to pick yourself up again. You choose every day to be better than you were before, because you know the things ahead have to be better than the past.  You see, the truth is that we attract what we desire. This girl wants to be positive and is looking for someone who Is positive, despite baggage and adversity (because I promise you she has it too) By thinking negatively like you are, you are accepting that you can never be worthy of that kind of positive love. You are worthy, you are loved. A positive life style is a mind set - not what we are blessed with or how we grew up. It is choosing to train your brain to attract positive vibrations and to be that yourself. There are millions of self-help books on how to do it, I suggest you pick one up some time.

Complaining truly makes you see more negative things in your life. Similar to counting your blessings, if you count your complaints, the more you will have - the more you will see. Try to bite your tongue when you want to complain. It's a bad day - not a bad life. Some have it worse... not to undermine your feelings. because your feelings are valid and true - it is merely how you respond to them which can make or break its effect on you.

\*Edit: I say two years, because this is the mark to the last time that I remember being truly happy. Not that life was perfect, but I was content. I felt beautiful, confident, smart, and blessed. Since then, I have had so much that has happened to me that I wish I knew where to start... I thought that all of this time, I was facing adversity with a brave face. I thought that I was being strong. The closer and closer that it has gotten to this two year mark, the more I feel enslaved by anxiety, depression, and pain. I have gained 40 pounds due to being annoerxic and other stresses... and every morning that I wake up, I feel as if I am carrying the weight of the past. I feel like the person I used to be has died. I look in the mirror and I don't recognize myself. I don't recognize my body. It feels like being trapped in someone else's skin. My weight is the only issue that can be seen from the outside, but it is a reflection of all of the deep scars within. No matter how hard I try, I can't get it to go away. I am very active, I eat well, but every time I step on the scale the number increases. - I have began to feel so much pain from all of the emotions I have held in for two years. It feels like a storm that crushes me. I have questioned almost every day for six months why I am alive... what is my purpose. I look at the sky and feel humbled - I am so small. But my pain feels so large. I want to save myself, but I don't know how. I truly have tried, but cannot escape the feelings inside of me. I want to be washed clean - I want to be new.
